headline: Tech stocks took a hammering last night while the ASX held firm today, with oil surging on Middle East tensions giving FUEL.AX a nice lift.

portfolio.summary: A tale of two markets today. Your ASX holdings — CBA, FUEL, VDHG, and VTS — all closed in the green, with FUEL leading the charge on surging oil prices. Your US tech stocks (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO) all fell sharply last night, with Microsoft dropping over 4% and Google close behind. Those US moves happened last night and won't hit your portfolio until tonight's US session reopens.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Dropped $19.21 to $441.31 USD last night — the biggest mover in your portfolio. The sell-off appears linked to broader tech weakness, though Morgan Stanley recently flagged strong AI revenue outlook. IBD noted it had 'retaken a key level' after a prior earnings dip, so this pullback stings a bit.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Fell $14.52 to $361.85 USD last night. Sentiment around Google has been rough — commentary is circulating that it's lagging behind OpenAI and Anthropic in the AI race, and that the shift to standalone AI apps could be a structural headwind for its core search business.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Best ASX performer today, up 1.75% to $8.70. Oil prices surged over 2% last night as US-Iran strikes and Israel-Lebanon conflict rattled Middle East supply fears. The IEA also warned of critically low stockpiles heading into peak summer demand — all bullish for energy stocks.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank
movers.note: Solid close at $164.76, up $1.76 today. No specific news driving it — CBA continues to ride broad ASX strength. The ASX 200 gained 0.7% today.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Down 2% to $222.38 USD last night. GTA 6 buzz continues — Rockstar's boss publicly insisted review scores still matter, and a YouTuber apparently tried to break into Rockstar's studio looking for leaks. Entertaining, but not the kind of news that moves the stock positively.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Quietly up 0.66% to $76.65 today — a steady result reflecting the ASX's broad gains. No specific news; just the market doing its thing.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a good day, closing up 0.7% at 8,785 — a solid 61-point gain. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 and NASDAQ were basically flat (up 0.1% each), so it wasn't a strong lead-in, but local conditions carried the ASX through. Oil was the big mover — WTI crude jumped over 2% to $95.69/barrel on Middle East conflict fears. Gold was steady. The Aussie dollar sat flat at 71.64 US cents.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Near-flat last night despite big drops in individual tech names

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Surging on Iran-US strikes and Middle East supply fears

politics.summary: The big economic story today is Australia's GDP growth print — the economy is expanding at 2.5% annually but showing signs of slowing. That's feeding into debate about whether the RBA (Reserve Bank) will keep hiking interest rates or hold off. Separately, Labor's budget headaches continue with MPs reportedly being asked to chip in for a campaign to defend the budget.

stories.title: Australia's economy growing at 2.5% annually but a slowdown is beginning
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's economy is growing at 2.5% per year, but the pace is slowing. For everyday Aussies, a softer economy generally means the RBA has less reason to keep raising interest rates — which matters enormously for mortgage holders. Watch for more detail on what sectors are dragging.

stories.title: Why stalling economy could stop further rate hikes
stories.why_it_matters: With the economy losing steam, analysts are now questioning whether the RBA will deliver further rate hikes. Traders are recalibrating — if the central bank hits pause, that's relief for mortgage holders and potentially bullish for bank stocks like CBA. This is the key macro story to watch this week.

stories.title: RBA and Chalmers blame interest rates and tax for house price falls
stories.why_it_matters: Both the RBA and Treasurer Chalmers are pointing fingers at interest rates and tax settings as reasons house prices are falling. It's unusual to see the central bank and the government publicly align on the cause — suggests there may be policy moves ahead to address the housing market. Property investors should take note.

stories.title: Labor MPs asked to fund campaign to salvage budget
stories.why_it_matters: Labor MPs are reportedly being asked to personally contribute to a campaign defending the federal budget — a sign the government is under real political pressure over its fiscal position. This kind of internal fundraising push suggests the budget narrative is proving harder to sell to voters than Canberra hoped.

ai.summary: The big AI themes today are Google's growing strategic vulnerabilities versus OpenAI and Anthropic, a new study showing all major AI models fail a specific type of security attack, and Trump's new AI executive order potentially reshaping how companies like Google and OpenAI launch models in the US.

stories.title: Google is lagging behind OpenAI and Anthropic — and it could be company-destroying
stories.source: Crypto Briefing (via M.G. Siegler / Big Technology)
stories.why_it_matters: Prominent tech analyst M.G. Siegler argues Google is falling dangerously behind OpenAI and Anthropic in the AI race. The key concern: as users shift from Google Search to standalone AI apps (like ChatGPT), Google's entire ad revenue model gets threatened. Siegler calls the strategic missteps potentially 'company-destroying' — strong language, and it's reflected in GOOGL's share price dropping nearly 4% last night. This is the core bear case for your GOOGL holding right now.

stories.title: All major AI models — OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Amazon, xAI — fail a specific type of cyberattack
stories.why_it_matters: A new study found that every major AI system — including ChatGPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google), Claude (Anthropic), and others — fails against a particular category of attack. The study doesn't name a single winner, meaning this is an industry-wide vulnerability. For investors in any of these companies, it's a reminder that AI safety and security remain unsolved problems that could attract regulatory attention or erode user trust.

stories.title: Trump's new AI executive order could change how OpenAI, Google and Anthropic launch models
stories.why_it_matters: Trump has signed a new AI executive order that could require AI companies to follow specific safety or disclosure processes before releasing new models. The details are still emerging, but it could slow down the pace at which Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic can ship new products — which matters if you're betting on any of these companies staying ahead in the AI race. WIRED separately reported the Trump administration is internally divided on how hard to push AI regulation.

stories.title: Google competing for $80 billion in investor money that could have gone to big AI IPOs
stories.why_it_matters: With major AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic preparing for potential IPOs (sharemarket listings), Google is suddenly in an unusual spot — it's competing for the same pool of investor dollars. If big AI IPOs suck up $80 billion in capital, some of that money could flow out of GOOGL shares. It's an interesting structural risk for existing Google shareholders.

sport.summary: NRL Round 14 is locked and loaded — the first game is tomorrow night (Sea Eagles vs Rabbitohs at 4 Pines Park). There's plenty of mid-season chatter about team form, trade targets, and a shock cross-code story. The AFL also had some news today worth noting.

stories.title: Round 14 team lists confirmed — every club's lineup revealed
stories.why_it_matters: All 17 clubs (Warriors on bye) have locked in their Round 14 squads. Kick-off is tomorrow night — Sea Eagles host the Rabbitohs at 4 Pines Park (7:50 PM). The Broncos host the Titans on Saturday night at Suncorp — the local Gold Coast interest game of the round.

stories.title: Mid-season report card: Staggering reality for fallen contenders — Ryles can't hide from the truth
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports dropped its mid-season NRL grades today, with some clubs — including a 'fallen contender' — copping brutal assessments. Raiders coach Ryles is reportedly facing uncomfortable truths about his team's season. No specific scores or club grades available from the article text, but it's a good read heading into Round 14.

stories.title: 'I'll never be loyal to a club': Tigers star's shock warning — and why Benji is at the centre
stories.why_it_matters: A Wests Tigers player has publicly declared he'll 'never be loyal to a club' — a bold statement that puts coach Benji Marshall in an awkward spot. The Tigers face the Panthers in Sunday's Round 14 game. The timing of this controversy, days before a tough match, is not ideal for the club. No player name confirmed from the article text alone.

stories.title: The next Mailata? Ex-NRL hopeful signs $3m NFL deal
stories.why_it_matters: An ex-NRL player who didn't make it in rugby league has signed a $3 million NFL deal, drawing comparisons to Jordan Mailata (the former South Sydney Rabbitohs player who became a star offensive lineman for the Philadelphia Eagles). It's a feel-good cross-code story and a reminder that the pathway from NRL to NFL is becoming a real thing for big athletes.

stories.title: AFL mid-season report card: Best players, biggest shocks and more
stories.why_it_matters: AFL.com.au released its mid-season report cards covering every club's best players and biggest surprises so far in 2026. No specific details available from the article text, but a handy snapshot of where the season stands at the halfway mark.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: AI narrative turning bearish — hold, don't panic-sell
watch_today.detail: GOOGL dropped nearly 4% last night and the 'Google is losing the AI war' commentary is getting louder. The shift of users from Search to standalone AI apps (ChatGPT etc.) is a genuine long-term risk. That said, Google still has massive infrastructure, cash flow, and its own capable AI (Gemini). A 4% single-day drop doesn't change the long-term thesis — hold and watch how the AI story evolves over the next quarter.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Down 4% last night — still a solid long-term hold
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dropped $19 last night, its biggest move in your portfolio. No specific negative catalyst — this looks like broad tech sector rotation. Morgan Stanley remains bullish on MSFT's AI revenue (Azure + Copilot) and IBD noted it had retaken a key technical level. Nothing here changes the long-term case. Hold.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil surging on Middle East conflict — energy ETF well positioned
watch_today.detail: WTI crude jumped over 2% to $95.69/barrel on US-Iran strikes and Israel-Lebanon tensions. The IEA warned of critically low global oil stockpiles heading into peak summer demand. FUEL.AX responded with a 1.75% gain today. This geopolitical tailwind could persist — hold and watch. If oil breaks $100, there's more upside here.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision: economy slowing — relief for mortgage holders may be coming
watch_today.detail: Australia's GDP growth is at 2.5% and slowing, and multiple economists are now saying the RBA has little reason to hike further. If the RBA signals a pause or cut, that's broadly positive for Australian equities (especially CBA.AX) and household sentiment. Worth watching closely this week as commentary builds ahead of the next RBA meeting.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 release approaching — TTWO in focus
watch_today.detail: GTA 6 hype is building with Rockstar's boss publicly defending the importance of review scores and a fan literally trying to break into Rockstar's studio. The game is one of the most anticipated releases in gaming history — if reviews land well, TTWO could get a significant bump. Hold ahead of the release, but be aware the stock could be volatile around launch.
